title.narrative: Multi-Purpose Cash and Protection Support for Vulnerable HH in Conflict-Affected Areas in Renk County, Upper Nile State

description.narrative: The project aims to address the urgent needs of Sudanese refugees, returnees, and internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Renk County, Upper Nile State, by combining emergency food security support with protection services, particularly GBV prevention and response. It targets critical gaps in humanitarian funding and prioritizes newly arrived refugees at the transit centre and vulnerable populations in host communities. Since 2023, Upper Nile has received over 1.1 million people from Sudan, with 1,400 new arrivals crossing into Renk daily. By July 2025, the transit centre population exceeded 12,400, with 79% being women and children. Between May and August 2024, UNHCR reported 126,012 arrivals, comprising 31% Sudanese refugees and 69% South Sudanese returnees. Renk is currently classified as IPC Phase 4 (Crisis), with projections indicating deterioration to Phase 5 (Emergency) or Phase 6 (Catastrophe). Over half the population faces crisis-level food insecurity due to flooding, conflict, rising food prices (+67%), and currency devaluation. Malnutrition rates are alarming, with 17% of children under five and pregnant/lactating women affected. Many new arrivals lack necessities, increasing dependence on humanitarian aid.
